findings.message: The gate must use "conduct-file paths resolved from routing". The only existing resolver is inline in `__main__._core`: it runs Registry(config).candidates(route.tier, route.surface) over config.routing, keeps cli providers, and maps claude -> CLAUDE.md and everything else -> AGENTS.md. The fence is fixed by the plan to hostfiles, gates, config, and merge plus their tests, and excludes squatch/__main__.py. The gate is therefore forced either to hook a seam whose owning module is unfenced, or to copy the provider-to-filename mapping into a second resolver in hostfiles/gates. The copy breaks the no-dual-path rule and lets `core` and `core_drift` drift apart on which files they manage.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket

findings.message: `test_classifier_is_unreachable_from_production_gates` asserts that no module in squatch/ imports `classify` from squatch.hostfiles or makes any `.classify(...)` attribute call. Activating the gate makes the drift logic reachable from production, which contradicts this test. No acceptance criterion names the migration. Separately, `test_rendering_has_no_git_or_commit_effect` pins hostfiles' imports to exactly {hashlib, re, typing}. That constrains where the gate and its routing lookup can live, and the ticket does not say so.
